archive.summary: MIT researchers developed X-Hinges, software that helps design 3D-printed objects with built-in sensors. The tricky part is separating the sensors’ signals from interference caused by the wire-like connections around them. The tool places two different materials in the design to reduce that interference. The researchers describe objects such as lamps and gloves that respond to touch, as well as small robots and toys. It is an understandable electronics problem: make an object sense what someone is doing, then get a clear signal out of it.

archive.title: Russia and Ukraine agree to local ceasefire in Oleshky amid deepening humanitarian crisis
archive.summary: The White House has said that Russia and Ukraine have agreed to a ceasefire in the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky, where a deepening humanitarian crisis has left thousands of civilians struggling to survive. In a statement on Friday, the White House said both sides had agreed to halt all military operations in the city from 27 October to allow humanitarian aid deliveries and preparations for the evacuation of civilians. Residents of the southern Ukrainian city, which has been under Russian occupation since February 2022, have described increasingly desperate conditions amid severe shortages of food, water and electricity. An estimated 2,000 people remain in the city, with some reportedly forced to survive on weeds, boiled grass, bread and meagre rations.

archive.title: US judge orders Trump administration to halt noncitizen voting investigation
archive.summary: A federal judge in California has ordered the Trump administration to halt investigations in nine states into whether noncitizens are registered to vote. US district court judge Araceli Martínez-Olguín in Oakland found the government’s effort was relying on data that is full of errors and that it was leading to intimidation of groups performing voter assistance efforts. She said it should be halted until polls close on election day on 3 November. She put her ruling, which was made on Wednesday, on hold until Friday to give the administration a chance to appeal. The ruling applies to investigations in California, Connecticut, Georgia, Missouri, Nevada, New York, Pennsylvania, Washington and Wisconsin.
